bug_semantics: When providers.kubernetesCRD.allowCrossNamespace=false, Traefik rejects direct IngressRoute middleware refs that name another namespace, but createChainMiddleware still honors MiddlewareRef.namespace on spec.chain.middlewares[] and emits makeID(foreignNS, name) with no isNamespaceAllowed check. A principal who can write a local Chain CRD can therefore bind and apply another namespace's middleware (stripPrefix, headers, forwardAuth, etc.) onto routes in their own namespace, bypassing the documented CRD isolation boundary.
flaw_origin: The unrestricted nested-chain resolver was first written in PR #5290 member 75e0baf2 (2019-09-03): Chain was switched from dynamic []string names to MiddlewareRef and createChainMiddleware copied IngressRoute-style ns:=mi.Namespace; makeID(ns, name) with no isolation gate. Parent 261e7c17 still assigned &middleware.Spec wholesale and had no createChainMiddleware. Later 7ba907f (2020-12-10) added AllowCrossNamespace and makeMiddlewareKeys for IngressRoute refs but left the 2019 chain helper untouched; that leftover path is the CVE-2026-41174 bypass.

reasoning: CVE-2026-41174 / GHSA-xhjw-95fp-8vgq is a real, published isolation-bypass in the Kubernetes CRD provider: nested Chain middleware refs were never covered by allowCrossNamespace. The patched lines are the createChainMiddleware resolver that turns spec.chain.middlewares[].namespace into a foreign makeID. AI is judged only on the BIC commit object: human author Julien Salleyron, Traefik merge-bot committer, no AI trailers on 75e0baf2, 422d2cf3, or 770b3739. Therefore NOT_AI.
